articles.title: Women: was your autoimmune condition misdiagnosed?
articles.summary: We want to hear from women with autoimmune conditions who received an incorrect or delayed diagnosis. Hundreds of millions of people – roughly one in ten globally – are affected by autoimmune conditions, diseases in which the immune system attacks the body instead of defending it.
body: Research from Cambridge University and the University of East Anglia found women are 43% more likely than men to receive a psychiatric misdiagnosis, meaning an autoimmune issue is misdiagnosed as a psychiatric problem, and 74% more likely to receive a psychosomatic misdiagnosis, meaning symptoms are considered psychological or stress-induced rather than physical. Women also reported significantly longer periods between the onset of symptoms and receiving a diagnosis – one to two years, compared to less than three months for men.

articles.title: ‘The view from the Mournes was CS Lewis’s idea of Narnia’: how Northern Ireland inspired a magical kingdom
articles.summary: Ahead of Netflix’s Chronicles of Narnia dropping early next year, we discover the fantastical landscapes that fired the Belfast-born author’s imagination. On the gable walls of the tough, working-class streets of east Belfast, the mystical beasts of Narnia vie for brick space with balaclava-wearing…
body: Lewis was born in Dundela in 1898 in an attractive terrace house that has sadly since been demolished to be replaced by rather unattractive flats. But elsewhere in this part of the city, the Lewis connection is being built on and celebrated. CS Lewis Square is in the Holywood Arches neighbourhood and has a short walking trail featuring metal sculptures of Mr and Mrs Beaver, Mr Tumnus and other beloved characters from The Chronicles of Narnia. The centrepiece is a gigantic Aslan, towering over all from atop a circular mound.

About 15 minutes’ walk away, St Mark’s church on the Holywood Road is the proud custodian of a much smaller lion that may have inspired Lewis’s creation of Aslan. His grandfather, the Rev Thomas Hamilton, ministered here, living in the rectory for 13 years, and his front door was decorated with a beautiful brass lion’s head doorknob. The original has been removed for safekeeping, but an exact replica attracts thousands of Lewis pilgrims each year.

articles.title: The pest I’ll never forget: the rats stood six or seven deep on the lawn beside my dormitory
articles.summary: All it took was one or two careless teenage girls giving the vermin a taste of their snacks and they became the most well-fed animals imaginable. I’ve written a fair amount about my boarding school years in Nigeria in the 90s, but never about the rats that accompanied my school experience.
body: I will never forget the sight of rats – six or seven deep – congregating at dusk on the scraggly lawn next to my dormitory, like an illegal gathering of political dissidents. They were large (what with their rich diet), thick tails twitching, noses pushed together, damn near whispering. At first, they would scatter when humans approached. Then we had to clap and stomp to get them to shift. Like the proletariat, the rats began to understand their power, and stand their ground. They were no longer pests but now a sort of predator. If this sounds like the beginning of a highbrow horror, that’s how it felt.

These rats were of course in their own habitat, perfectly at home, and adapting to our unwelcome presence. We were the interlopers, with our classrooms and dormitories, and daily assemblies and annual sports days. I can now recognise that dealing with a certain kind of pest is a fact of life in places where nature has not yet been completely decimated. The rats were the price of a kind of freedom. But years later, post-pandemic lockdown, when the rats attempted to colonise New York, I had searing flashes of the rats of my childhood. Yup, still traumatising.
points: All it took was one or two careless teenage girls giving the vermin a taste of their snacks and they became the most well-fed animals imaginable.

articles.title: Fritters and chocolate cake: Thomasina Miers’ recipes for cooking with pumpkin
articles.summary: Quick, simple finger food that children will love for Halloween: pumpkin and carrot fritters with a chilli-coriander relish, and pumpkin baked into a dark chocolate slice. It would be lazy to write, with a rueful shake of the head, that Halloween gets bigger every year. Halloween is huge.
body: Delightfully crisp, rich in flavour and delicately spiced, these are simple to throw together but look and taste spectacular, especially with the zippy relish for dipping.
Coarsely grate the pumpkin and carrot, then wrap them in a clean tea towel or kitchen paper, and squeeze hard to push out any excess moisture.

Put a frying pan on a medium heat, add the oil and spring onions, and cook, stirring, for two to three minutes. Grind the coriander and cumin seeds in a mortar, then add to the pan with the cinnamon and a few generous pinches of salt, and cook for a few minutes more. Add the garlic and ginger, and cook, stirring all the time, for a couple of more minutes. By now, the onions will have softened and the mixture will be smelling irresistibly fragrant. Tip the lot into a large bowl, then add the grated pumpkin and carrots, and the gram flour. Season with a little more salt and plenty of black pepper, then mix to combine.

articles.title: How to Create a Wellness Device That Sells — and Sticks
articles.summary: What separates a bestselling wellness device from a passing fad? Healf, Suri, Therabody, Eight Sleep and Bon Charge share their secrets for cutting through the noise and driving sales.
body: From massage guns and red light therapy panels to LED face masks and lymphatic drainage devices, consumers today can choose from hundreds of wellness gadgets promising to address every bodily concern, at every budget.

The overlap between beauty and wellness is growing by the day via at-home devices that promise medical-grade results. Gen Zs and millennials are most likely to spend on several at-home devices promising to optimize their musculoskeletal health, facial appearance, sleep, and recovery. You only need to log in to TikTok to get an idea of consumer demand — videos tagged with #RedLightTherapy have collectively amassed nearly 100 million views.

The global wellness economy is projected to keep growing rapidly to $9.8 trillion by 2029, up from $6.8 trillion in 2024, according to the Global Wellness Institute. Within that, the global LED face mask market is forecast to more than double from $304 million in 2026 to $679 million by 2034, according to Fortune Business Insights, while the sleep tech devices market is expected to more than triple from $30 billion in 2025 to $96.7 billion by 2032, according to Research and Markets.

articles.title: Beauty on the Move: The New Era of Travel Retail
articles.summary: With global travel retail sales falling, brands and retailers are rethinking everything from product mix to presentation. With foot traffic rising, will shoppers return?
body: More people than ever are traveling, but getting them to shop is proving harder. For beauty, one of travel retail’s biggest categories, recovery remains elusive.

Spanning airport duty-free stores, downtown duty-free shopping destinations, airlines and cruise ships, global travel retail is a vital sales and brand-building platform for beauty, offering access to millions of international travelers. Fragrance dominates sales in Western markets, while skincare has traditionally driven demand in North Asia, particularly among Chinese shoppers. In the Middle East, luxury fragrance and gifting are major draws. Beauty accounted for the largest share of the $76 billion global duty-free and travel retail market in 2025, at 32.2%, according to Generation Research.

articles.title: Inside the New D.C. Restaurant That Only Sells Five Curry Steak Frites Every Night
articles.summary: The hottest new spot in Washington, D.C. focuses on the traditional heat-packed cooking methods of northern Thailand, while still using local ingredients from around the DMV.
body: Elsewhere in the kitchen, another chef carves green papayas. The irregular slices of papaya get tossed in a funky, spicy dressing for each order. Ko calls it the “most labor intensive dish on the line;” each order is carefully mixed with fresh tomatoes, peanuts, and a palm syrup and tamarind-heavy dressing. A rich pork belly curry is simmering in the background. Gaeng hung lay (a traditional northern Thai curry) cooks down large pieces of pork belly to get that fatty layer, with pickled garlic and pineapple balancing out the rich flavors of curry paste, tamarind, and fish sauce.

Right before service, the chefs begin prepping herbs and sticky rice that has been soaking overnight and is quickly steamed for that malleable, glutinous texture. McCoy talks about how being a chef is more of a lifestyle than a job, but there’s immense payoff when you get to see diners enjoy your hard work every night. He hopes that Alfie’s will become a place where “you can just forget where you are, have a good time, and just lose yourself in the experience and the food.”
Watch the kitchen team at Aflie’s cook classic Thai dishes and fusion plates like curry steak frites in this episode of Now Open.

And while they’re in everything from supplements to IVs, the best peptide serums stand apart for their ability to boost hydration, increase collagen and elastin, and deliver smoother, more youthful skin—with the evidence to back up many of their claims.

But even in skincare, these ingredients are enjoying newfound attention. “ Peptides have graduated from the fine print to the front of the bottle,” says Mona Gohara, MD, a board-certified dermatologist in Hamden, Connecticut. They’re quickly approaching hyaluronic acid -territory—which itself has become a household name—in part due to their versatility. “Many peptide formulas offer improvements in the appearance of fine lines and firmness while being relatively easy to tolerate and incorporate into a routine,” she says. “They also pair beautifully with ingredients such as hyaluronic acid, niacinamide, and antioxidants.”

While hunting for the perfect Airbnb, I've been fantasizing about future winter trips to the continent: waking to the snow-dusted Dolomites, cozying up in centuries-old lodges in the Alps post- après-ski, or exploring lesser-known Nordic slopes where the northern lights put on a colorful show after dark.

Some of the European Airbnbs for ski trips below are so spectacular, they're worth planning an entire winter vacation around.
